function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

**Where to Order a Cake – A Quick Guide** Below is a mix of local‑shop options, national chains, and online specialty sites that let you order a cake (fresh, pre‑baked, or custom‑made). Pick the one that best fits your budget, style, and delivery needs. | Category | What to Look For | Example Sites / Stores | Tips | |----------|------------------|------------------------|------| | **Local Bakeries** | Fresh, hand‑crafted, often customizable | • *Your town’s top‑rated bakery* (search “best bakery near me”)
• *Bakeries that accept phone orders* | • Call ahead for availability & delivery times.
• Ask about “no‑show” policies if you’re ordering for a surprise. | | **National Chains** | Consistent quality, quick turnaround | • **Panera Bread** – “Panera Cakes” (online & in‑store)
• **Dunkin’** – “Dunkin’ Cakes” (online & in‑store)
• **Kraft Foods** – “Kraft Bakery” (online) | • Great for last‑minute orders.
• Check for local delivery or pickup options. | | **Online Specialty Shops** | Custom designs, gourmet flavors, often free shipping | • **Goldbelly** – “Order a cake from a famous bakery”
• **Bakeology** – “Custom cakes delivered”
• **Cake Boss** – “Custom cake design” | • Ideal for unique occasions (weddings, birthdays).
• Order at least 1–2 weeks in advance for custom work. | | **Grocery Delivery Services** | One‑stop shop, often includes cake options | • **Instacart** – “Cakes from local grocery”
• **Amazon Fresh** – “Bakery items”
• **Shipt** – “Bakery & dessert” | • Great if you’re already ordering groceries.
• Delivery windows are usually 1–3 hours. | | **Specialty Dessert Shops** | Artisan, vegan, gluten‑free, etc. | • **Vegan Cake Co.** – “Plant‑based cakes”
• **Gluten‑Free Bakery** – “GF cakes”
• **Dessert Café** – “Custom cupcakes & cakes” | • Perfect for dietary restrictions.
• Many offer “same‑day” delivery. | | **DIY Kits** | Make‑your‑own cake at home | • **Amazon** – “Cake baking kits”
• **Etsy** – “DIY cake kits” | • Fun for a personal touch.
• Great for parties where you want to involve guests. | ### How to Choose the Right Option 1. **Know Your Deadline** - *Same‑day*: Local bakeries or grocery delivery. - *Next‑day*: National chains or online shops with “next‑day” shipping. - *Custom design*: Order 2–4 weeks ahead. 2. **Consider Your Budget** - Local bakeries: $20–$50 for a standard 8‑inch cake. - National chains: $30–$70. - Specialty shops: $50–$150+ (custom, premium ingredients). 3. **Dietary Needs** - Vegan, gluten‑free, nut‑free, or sugar‑free options are widely available online. - Ask the bakery for ingredient lists if you have allergies. 4. **Delivery Logistics** - Confirm the delivery window and whether the cake needs refrigeration. - Some sites offer “delivery confirmation” via text or email. 5. **Reviews & Ratings** - Check Google, Yelp, or Trustpilot for recent customer feedback. - Look for photos of the finished product. ### Quick Order Checklist | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Decide on cake size, flavor, and design. | | 2 | Pick a vendor (local, chain, or online). | | 3 | Place the order (online or phone). | | 4 | Confirm delivery date/time and address. | | 5 | Pay (most sites accept credit card, PayPal, or Apple Pay). | | 6 | Receive confirmation & track delivery if available. | --- #### Need a Specific Recommendation? If you tell me your city or zip code, I can pull up the top-rated local bakeries or the best online options that deliver to your area. Just let me know!
